Maya (People Ops): Quick update — weve published a region-specific PTO guidance for religious observances and culturally important days. This lets people swap one standard PTO day per calendar year to cover a documented religious/cultural observance without using additional unpaid leave. Link: https://redwood.company/hr/pto-swap (policy + form)

Priyanka (People Ops): TL;DR: you can request a PTO swap up to 30 days before the date. Your manager and People Ops need to sign off. This is intended to reduce manual exceptions for commonly missed observed days across regions. :sparkles:

Aisha (Eng): great! does this affect local public holidays or only religious/cultural observances?

Maya (People Ops): Only for documented religious/cultural observances that are not already local public holidays. If it is a public holiday in your region, use the standard holiday calendar. If youre unsure, check the linked FAQ or ping people-ops.

Jon (Finance): Quick note — swapped days are treated as paid PTO for payroll purposes. No change to accrual. Finance will reconcile in monthly payroll; put the approved swap date in the form so we can map it.

Aisha (Eng): And the process? Manager approve + People Ops approve, right? Any exceptions for on-call folks?

Priyanka (People Ops): Correct. Steps: 1) Fill the swap form (link in the policy) 2) Manager approves in 5 business days 3) People Ops signs off. On-call: if youre on an active on-call rotation that week, we ask teams to ensure coverage; team lead can request a deferred swap (we have a checkbox).

Maya (People Ops): Form snippet for copy/paste: ```Form ID: PTO-SWAP-2026
Employee: <name>
Region: <country>
Requested swap date: <YYYY-MM-DD>
Observance name: <free text>
Documentation: <optional link or note>
Manager approval: <manager email>```

Aisha (Eng): what counts as documentation? a community calendar event, a faith organization page, brief note is fine?

Priyanka (People Ops): Brief note or link is usually sufficient. Were trying to avoid heavy administrative burden — well escalate only if something is unclear. Examples in the FAQ.

Jonas (People Ops): Heads up — there are blackout dates for swaps tied to major product launches and headcount freezes (listed in the policy). If your requested date falls in a blackout window, the form will flag it and People Ops will advise alternatives.

Aisha (Eng): can managers pre-approve a standing swap for recurring observances (e.g., annual)?

Maya (People Ops): Not automatically. We encourage employees to submit each year so the swap is explicit in payroll records. If teams want a local standing practice, please coordinate with People Ops and we can add a manual note to your team file.

hr-bot: People Ops form submitted by aisha@redwood — pending manager approval. (automated)

Aisha (Eng): thanks, filled it out.

Priyanka (People Ops): Thanks — well review within 3 business days. If anyone needs help with the form or the travel interplay (e.g., traveling to an observance), DM people-ops or drop in #help.

Jon (Finance): If youre traveling internationally to observe a holiday, remember travel reimbursements follow the normal travel policy — swaps do not change expense eligibility.

Maya (People Ops): Final note: this is a pilot for 12 months. Well collect feedback and report back at the Q3 all-hands. Please use the feedback field on the form or email people-ops+pto-swap@redwood.company. :pray:

Priyanka (People Ops): thanks everyone — tagging this for visibility and adding to the People Ops pinned posts. :pushpin:

Aisha (Eng): appreciated :heart:
